basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 2-3.' and it opens 'VERS. 2, 3.-- Cui respondit mulier: De fructu lignorum quae sunt in paradiso vescimur, et'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 2, 3.-- Cui respondit mulier: De fructu lignorum quae sunt in paradiso vescimur, et reliqua. Cur mulier ad interrogata serpenti [ Z., serpentis] | respondit? Ut praevaricatio ejus esset inexcusabilis, cum nullo modo dicere potuit se oblitam esse mandati, quod serpenti prodidit.
